plate.narration: Tall boundary stones stand across the caravan road. A dragonling grandmother lifts a little bell over a waiting pack. Behind her, wheels and tails crowd the red hills. Everyone wants through. The stones are in no hurry.

objectives.label: Got a prospector to listen to the one rule
Laid out the whole outline of the truth

goal.text: Get past the old boundary stones, and find out why they hold the rush back.

steps.label: Calm the crowd at the stones

facet_unassigned.name: The Unassigned Stone
facet_unassigned.text: Kept by the grandmothers with the list of caves never assigned. Don't you dare sell it.

scene_stones_line.narration: Your job: get past the old boundary stones, and find out why they hold the rush back. Tall gray stones lean across the road into the red hills. A crowd waits outside them. Somebody brought a chair. Somebody else brought a bigger chair.

scene_dragonling_home.narration: A grandmother with glasses on a chain drops her pencil. "Well! Look who came home the FRONT way." Four aunts hug you. Then her face goes serious. "Worst season in the tallies, love. Come and help."

scene_inspection.narration: At the gate, a dragonling grandmother passes a bell over each pack and tallies every ring. "No digging tools past the stones. Your turn." She adjusts her glasses, then her pencil, then her glasses again.

check_not_diggers.prompt: Turn out every pocket and lay your gear in one neat row, fast, so the grandmother can see there is not a pick or a shovel in it

onSuccess.narration: Rope, socks, a squashed sandwich, a spoon. Not one pick, not one shovel, and you never once say the word treasure. The grandmother taps her pencil on her teeth. "Not diggers," she writes. "Very tidy." She waves you through with a look that is almost respect.

onFailure.narration: You lay it all out, but your packs are still ringing like a shop door. The grandmother inspects everything anyway, including your socks, and writes PROBABLY HONEST in the tally book. Then she hugs you, because that is what grandmothers do after an inspection.

scene_inspection_open_packs.narration: The grandmother checks what you carry and tallies anything that hums. "The tally house will want your story." She sends you through, after checking your socks twice.

scene_inspection_show_charm.narration: You hold up the witch's charm. It rings with the grandmother's bell, the very same note. "That's Thrum's work!" she says. "Is that old crow still at the ford? Anybody Thrum trusts can skip my socks."

scene_gate_town.narration: In the gate town, bells hang from poles, from packs and from one goat. "Take what the mountain drops," says a grandmother. "Never pry at what it holds." A man with a huge pry bar says he did not hear. The goat heard.

scene_bell_code.narration: A small dragonling, the town's bell-code expert, explains very fast: one ring for moths leaving, two for a warm cave, three for come home now. There is an unrung bell too. Ask about that one, and she stops talking.

scene_gate_town_explain_home.narration: You plant your feet and say it exactly like your grandmother, finger wagging: "Take what the mountain drops. Never pry at what it holds. And wipe your feet." Every grandmother nods so hard her glasses bounce.

check_one_rule.prompt: Act out the one rule for a stubborn prospector: pick up a fallen pebble nice and easy, then pry at the hill and get flattened

onSuccess.narration: You do not shout the rule at him. You act it out: pick up a pebble the mountain dropped, nice and easy, then pretend to pry at the hill, and pretend the hill sits on you. You fall over flat, very slowly, like a tree. Somewhere in the middle he stops saying "right, right" and starts actually watching.

onFailure.narration: He watches the whole thing, nods along, says "Right, right," and marches off up the hill with his pry bar anyway. You follow him, because somebody should.

scene_rule_heard.narration: The prospector gives up his pry bar. A grandmother hangs it on a wall of hundreds. "Every one of those listened, in the end." She finds a hook between two very stubborn ones.

scene_crab_warning.narration: Up the hill, the prospector is about to pry at a sparkling heap on warm ground. The heap stands up. It is a glassback crab, doing a slow, clacking dance, claws raised. Its friend stands up too.

check_read_crab.prompt: Read what the glassback crab's dance means

onSuccess.narration: Claws up. Sideways shuffle. Rock to the left. You have seen a cat do something very like it on a warm wall, and you know exactly what the cat meant.

onFailure.narration: You decide the dance means hello. It does not mean hello.

scene_crab_settles.narration: Claws up and a sideways shuffle means: this warm ground is my house. Everybody steps back slowly. The crabs settle down and go back to looking like a very expensive pile of gems. The prospector hands you his pry bar.

encounter_crabs.narration: The glassback crabs charge, slow and clacking and very sure of themselves.

onVictory.narration: The crabs back into their warm burrow, still clacking. The prospector drops his pry bar and runs all the way back past the stones.

onDefeat.narration: The crabs chase you down the hill, past the bells, and right back out through the boundary stones.

scene_crabs_rescue.narration: Out past the stones, the grandmothers fish you out of the heather, one collar at a time. They bandage your scrapes. "Bandages cost, this season," says one, over her glasses. Up the hill, the crabs clack, very pleased with themselves.

scene_crabs_rescue_pay.narration: You count two coins into a grandmother's palm. She bites each one, writes BANDAGES: PAID, and gives everybody a hard candy for being brave. The coins are gone, and so is the afternoon.

scene_crabs_rescue_supper.narration: You hand over your supper. Eleven grandmothers share it out, a crumb each, and declare it adequate. It was going to be a lovely supper. Your tummies grumble all the way back to the stones.

scene_crabs_rescue_work.narration: The grandmothers keep a wall of pry bars, each one given up by somebody who listened in the end. More wait to be hung. You hang them until your arms ache: one hundred and six. The afternoon is gone.

scene_turned_back.narration: Outside the stones, turned-back prospectors sit on benches. Wend, the kind ladler from the north road, serves them soup under a DEEP HOLLOW flap, and remembers your names. A box on the pot reads FOR THE ROOT OF THINGS.

check_ask_wend.prompt: Get a straight answer out of Wend

onSuccess.narration: Wend thinks for a long time. "Everything that hums wants to go home," Wend says at last. "We'd like to help it get there, all at once." It sounds lovely. It also sounds like something nobody should do on a guess. You go up to the tally house thinking about it.

onFailure.narration: Wend answers a different question, beautifully, about the right amount of salt in soup. By the end you know a great deal about salt and nothing at all about roots. Wend waves you off to the tally house with a full bowl.

scene_turned_back_share_soup.narration: You squeeze onto a bench between two turned-back prospectors. They grumble about grandmothers, then talk about home. By the second bowl, they are talking about going there. Wend learns every name.

scene_turned_back_said_no.narration: "We said no," you tell Wend, "on the north road." Wend nods. "I remember." Wend fills your bowls anyway, just as warmly. "Soup's still free. Kindness first." The crystal hums the same note as your packs.

scene_turned_back_coin.narration: Wend hugs everybody and shows the tent your names in the little book. "These ones helped," Wend says, and everybody claps. It is very warm in the tent. You are not sure you like it.

scene_tallies.narration: In the tally house, Great-Grandma Ashby, the oldest grandmother of all, opens a big book full of tidy eruption marks. This season's page is mostly question marks. "Show me what you know," she says, tapping her walking stick. "We will compare."

scene_tallies_hear_tallies.narration: Ashby reads the old rhythm: moons, a small gemfall, moons again, for a thousand years. Then she reads this season's broken one. Somebody has drawn a very worried face in the margin.

scene_charm_rings.narration: The witch's charm rings the moment you hold it up. Ashby goes very still. She opens the oldest book and points to a mark like a little bell. "Same note. My great-great-grandma heard it too."

scene_verses_sung.narration: You sing the spiral verses. The grandmothers lay a string on the floor map, landmark by landmark. The roads curl around the gemfalls just like their tally marks. One grandmother says a word not allowed in the tally house.

check_outline.narration: Ashby puts chalk in your hand and taps the clues on the floor map, one at a time. "Watch," she says. "Then put them back the same way. Slowly, dears."

interaction.cue: Watch the clues light up, then chalk them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: The note every stone hums, the curling songs, the quiet jackalopes, the broken tallies: you chalk them down in order, and the shape is plain.

onFailure.narration: You muddle the pieces. Ashby moves the chalk marks with her stick, humming, until the shape is plain.

onAssisted.narration: Ashby taps the last clue once with her stick, and the shape is plain: the note every stone hums, the curling songs, the quiet jackalopes, the broken tallies.

scene_here_first.narration: "One more thing," says Ashby. "The boundary stones were here first. Before the first families. Already marking the line we mark now." Everything you have seen points one way: the stones are older than the mountain's name, and the land has always kept count.

check_read_stone.prompt: Read the worn marks on the oldest boundary stone

onSuccess.narration: On the oldest stone, under the moss, are rows of marks worn almost smooth. They are tally marks, like the grandmothers' marks, but far older. Somebody was counting here before the first families came. The land has been keeping records. Great-Grandma Ashby only nods. "Now come and see my shelf."

onFailure.narration: The marks are worn so smooth you cannot tell scratches from weather. Great-Grandma Ashby takes your hand and runs your fingers along them: one, one, one, and a gap. "Counting," she says. "Before us. Come and see the shelf."

scene_here_first_onward.narration: On a shelf behind Ashby, something glints. She sees you looking. "Clever eyes," she says. She reaches up with her stick, as gently as you would touch a sleeping baby's blanket. "Come here, then. Carefully."

scene_unassigned.narration: A fresh-fallen gem rests on an old list of caves nobody may gather in. "Keeping," says Ashby. "Not hiding." Her stick straightens the list without touching the gem. You could ask to carry it north, as proof.

scene_unassigned_leave_kept.narration: You leave the stone on its list. Ashby squares the paper with her stick. "Some things want keeping more than carrying." The shelf hums softly behind you.

scene_unassigned_ask_proper.narration: You hold a warm rock in both hands and ask the proper way, the way every dragonling child learns. Ashby presses her lips tight. Then she sets the gem on top of your rock. "Keeping. Not taking. Don't you dare sell it."

check_carry.prompt: Lift the gem off its list the keeping way: two hands, slow as a snail, and set the list straight again after

onSuccess.narration: Two hands, slow as a snail, and you square the list after with one finger. Great-Grandma Ashby wraps the gem in a page torn from nothing important and puts it in your hands. "The Unassigned Stone. Keep it. Don't you dare sell it."

onFailure.narration: Your fingers bump the list crooked, and you grab at the gem as if it might run off. Great-Grandma Ashby pats your hand. "You'll know the difference soon. Not today." The stone stays on its list, and somehow that feels right too.

scene_moths_leaving.narration: Embermoths stream south over the porch. A bell rings once. The town's bell-code expert, a dragonling of about six, tugs your sleeve. "One ring. Moths leaving," she says. "Every night this month."

check_follow_moths.prompt: Everybody run to keep up with a river of embermoths

onSuccess.narration: You run along the hillside under the glowing river. The moths do not drift at random. They flow around every cave where a stone has fallen, the way water flows around a rock, and then carry on south. You come back out of breath, with sparks in your hair.

onFailure.narration: You run, trip over a goat, and lie on your back in the heather watching the moths go over. From down there it is the most beautiful thing you have ever seen. The goat lies down too. Neither of you says anything for a while.

scene_moths_leaving_hold_one.narration: An embermoth lands in your hands, warm as cocoa. Then it notices your pack. It lifts off and loops wide around the humming thing inside, then flies south with the others. The small dragonling pats your arm. "They all do that."

scene_moths_leaving_ask_bells.narration: "They always leave a little before the mountain wakes," says the small dragonling, very fast, "and come back after. Grandmothers count everything." She frowns. "But never this many. And they haven't come back."

scene_bell_house_supper.narration: Supper in the bell house is a long table, forty grandmothers, and bread baked on hot rocks. Ashby taps the table. "Old rule. Every guest brings something: a story, a recipe, a thing from the road." Forty pairs of glasses turn your way.

check_supper_story.prompt: Tell forty grandmothers a good story

onSuccess.narration: You tell them about the lines and the jackalopes and the roads that bend, and you do all the voices. Forty grandmothers laugh in the right places and gasp in the right places, and one of them cries a little at the end, and says it is the onions.

onFailure.narration: You get the order muddled and tell the end first. The grandmothers do not mind at all. They simply tell it back to you in the right order, interrupting each other, until it is a much better story than the one you started with.

scene_bell_house_supper_ask_recipe.narration: Ask forty grandmothers for one recipe, and you get forty recipes and an argument that lasts until dessert. They agree on one thing: you are far too thin. You go to bed with a pile of loaves.

scene_bell_house_supper_depot_tag.narration: You set the Depot Stone on the table. The bell house goes silent. Ashby holds up its SOLD tag with two fingers, as if it smells. "Nobody sells what the mountain drops." She drops the tag in the fire. "Now you're keeping it. Not owning it."

rest_bell_house.narration: Sleep on warm stone under silent bells. A grandmother adds a hot rock to your blanket. Outside, the rush still lines up by lantern light. Inside, even the smallest bell is tucked in.

scene_night_lights.narration: The bell-code expert shakes you awake. Three lanterns bob up toward a hillside cave. "That cave's on the list," she whispers. "Nobody gathers there." Her slippers are on the wrong feet.

check_night_talk.prompt: Talk three night diggers out of a cave

onSuccess.narration: Halfway up you find three young prospectors with lanterns and one shovel. You sit down on a rock with them and tell them about the list, and the one rule, and the grandmothers' bells. They go a bit pale. "We thought it was just a cave," says one. They walk back down with you, and nobody digs.

onFailure.narration: You climb up quietly, step on a bell somebody left in the heather, and it goes CLANG. The three diggers drop everything and run straight back down to the stones. Their shovel stays behind. A grandmother collects it at dawn and hangs it on the wall where the grandmothers keep every pry bar anybody ever gave up.

scene_night_lights_wake_grans.narration: Eleven grandmothers march uphill in nightgowns, ringing hand bells. The lanterns wobble, then flee downhill. Ashby comes back yawning. "Thank you, dears. Back to bed."

scene_night_lights_fly_look.narration: Your griffin glides up without a sound. The lanterns belong to three young prospectors with one shovel and no idea where they are. You point them back toward the stones. They say thank you, and do not dig.

scene_morning_bells.narration: At dawn, the bell-code expert has jobs. "Learn the big-bell crew's passing line," she says, very fast, "or polish hand bells for a chorus. Both help at the stones!" The bell in the corner hangs untouched, its rope tied high.

check_big_bell.prompt: Everybody haul on the rope of the biggest bell in the bell house

onSuccess.narration: You haul on the rope. The bell swings, and BONG, the whole hillside hums, and you feel it in your teeth. Far up the hills, other bell houses answer, one after another. The small dragonling says that was very nearly as good as a grandmother.

onFailure.narration: You haul on the rope, and the bell swings, and the rope swings back up and takes you with it. For one glorious moment you are flying. Then the grandmothers catch you, one on each ankle, and the bell rings anyway, louder than ever.

scene_morning_bells_polish.narration: You polish the hand bells until your faces look stretched and silly in them. The expert teaches you where each note fits. She calls the little chorus acceptable. This is her highest mark.

scene_morning_bells_unrung.narration: The small dragonling, who has talked nonstop since yesterday, stops. "Nobody rings that one," she says quietly. "Not ever. Great-Grandma says we'll know." She touches its rim on tiptoe. It is cold, in a house of warm stones.

scene_crowd_at_stones.narration: At the stones, the morning crowd is pushing. A man in a feathered hat shouts from a cart that they are only rocks. "Not one step back, dears," say the grandmothers. Help make room, share what you know, or use your bell job.

check_tell_crowd.prompt: Get a shouting crowd to listen

onSuccess.narration: You climb up beside the feathered hat and tell them: the hum, the silent warrens, the roads that bend, the moths going south. You tell it like a story, because it is one. The crowd goes quiet. The feathered hat comes off. Nobody pushes after that.

onFailure.narration: You climb up and start to tell them, and the crowd shouts you down. But while they are shouting at you, nobody is pushing. By the time they run out of breath, the grandmothers have rung for help, and twenty more grandmothers have arrived. The crowd sits down, grumbling.

choice_crowd_at_stones_stand_with.narration: You stand in the line between two grandmothers and say nothing at all. The crowd looks at them, at you, and at the old stones. The feathered hat climbs down, muttering. It is hard to push past people just standing there, being right.

choice_crowd_at_stones_sing_verses.narration: You sing Old Corran's spiral verses from the top of a stone. Half the crowd sings along. Then come the new verses, the ones that bend away and away. The voices trail off. They have walked those bends.

scene_centaur_whisper.narration: With the crowd calm, a centaur guide named Perrin Nine-Verse beckons you behind a stone. "There's a Shortcut through the hills," he whispers. "My family has argued about it for nine generations. Will you walk it?"

scene_shortcut.narration: The Shortcut is real. It runs through a crack in a hill and comes out at the last boundary stone, a whole day ahead. Perrin has tears in his eyes. "Never tell anyone," he says. "It's the best argument we've got."

scene_centaur_whisper_caravan_road.narration: You choose the caravan road. Perrin is so relieved he has to sit down. "Good! The argument lives," he says. "My grandfather would be furious if it ended on a Tuesday." He gallops off to argue with someone.

scene_centaur_whisper_show_bark.narration: Perrin reads Old Corran's bark, lips moving. Then he goes pale. "Corran's new verses bend around the Shortcut too. It's been in the song all along." He hands it back with shaking hooves. "Don't tell Corran."

scene_warden_count.narration: At the last stone, Sergeant Holloway from the north road has a ledger open. "You again. Good. I need counters. Picks going north: four hundred and twelve. Picks back: nine. I dislike this arithmetic."

check_count_picks.prompt: Count every pick in a moving crowd

onSuccess.narration: You count, and count, and your number matches the sergeant's exactly. Holloway writes your names in the ledger under 'Counters, Reliable,' which is apparently a great honor. "The citadel keeps logs," the sergeant says. "Somebody has to."

onFailure.narration: You count four hundred and twelve picks, two goats and a very tall hat. Holloway checks your sums, crosses out the goats, keeps the hat, and writes you down as 'Counters, Enthusiastic.' "Close enough," says the sergeant. "For arithmetic."

scene_warden_count_ask_logs.narration: "We write it down," says Holloway. "Every pick, every ash wind, every moth night. It all goes up to Redspire and onto a shelf." The sergeant closes the ledger. "Mostly, nobody reads it."

scene_warden_count_sky_news.narration: Your griffin and the sergeant swap sky news: ash over the peak every evening, moths flying south, warm wind where it should be cold. Holloway writes it all down. "Same as our logs," the sergeant says quietly.

scene_who_to_tell.narration: Ashby meets you at the stone. "Who hears what you found first?" she asks. "The Skywardens keep logs at their citadel. We grandmothers can ring it through the bell towns. Or you can keep it close." She taps her stick and waits.

scene_who_to_tell_ring_home.narration: You ring your family's bell, the pattern you learned before you could talk. From three towns up the hills, a bell rings it back, then adds the one for hurry home for supper. Ashby pretends very hard not to hear.

scene_tell_wardens.narration: A relay runner carries your story to the Skywardens. Ashby sniffs. "They do write things down." She checks that the runner's cord is tied properly.

scene_tell_gatherers.narration: The grandmothers ring your news from town to town. Ashby blows her nose very loudly and says it is a cold. Nobody asks why she is smiling.

scene_keep_close.narration: You keep what you found to yourselves. Ashby nods. "Careful is not the same as quiet. But careful is a start." The bells ring their ordinary morning rings.

end_through_the_stones.narration: You walk north through the boundary stones into the foothills, with the rush all around you. Ahead, on a red ridge, stands the Skywardens' citadel. Tonight you camp under the stones that were here first. They feel like they are on your side.

variants.text: Your morning bell job gave the crowd room.

interaction_pry_bars.narration: You and the prospectors carry their pry bars to the grandmothers' wall, where every tool given up at the stones is hung. A grandmother counts three coins into your hands. "Wall-hanging rate. Honest work, honestly paid."

interaction_bell_cart.narration: The grandmothers wheel their loudest hand bell down to the stones on a little cart. A wheel sticks in a rut. "Somebody steer!" calls the bell-code expert. "Everybody push!"

interaction.cue: Friends push the cart while someone steers it out of the rut.

onSuccess.narration: The wheel pops out with a CLUNK, and the bell gives one happy ring. The bell-code expert rides the rest of the way on top, bossing the goats.

onFailure.narration: The cart tips. BONG. A grandmother lifts the whole thing out of the rut with one hand and says nothing at all.

scene_crawlers_porch.narration: On the porch, the hum in your packs jumps. Bone crawlers scuttle out from under the boards, small, pale and many-legged. They love a hum, and they are heading for the tally house books, the best nest a crawler ever saw. "Not in my books!" says Ashby. "Shoo them, dears."

encounter_crawlers.narration: The crawlers click across the porch, straight for the humming packs and the tally house door. Drive them off before they reach the books.

scene_crawlers_shooed.narration: The crawlers scuttle away under the porch in one tidy line. Ashby counts her books twice. Then she hands you a little brass whistle. "One loud note. Crawlers hate it. So do I." The first stars are coming out.

scene_crawlers_scattered.narration: The crawlers swarm your boots. Then every grandmother comes out ringing a hand bell, and the crawlers pop back under the boards. No whistle tonight, but the books are safe. The first stars are coming out.

scene_bell_house_supper_honey.narration: You put a coin on the table. A grandmother carries in a pot of honey the size of her head. It goes on bread, on porridge, and once, by mistake, on a glasses case. She slides a honeycake into your pack. "For the road."

interaction_bell_tuck.narration: You help Ashby wrap the bells in soft cloths. One gives a tiny ting, and the grandmothers answer with a soft shhh. A grandmother tucks leftover bread into your pack. "Breakfast," she whispers.

interaction_gear_inventory.narration: Lay out what you carry and say what each thing is for. The grandmother checks beside you. One sock has been mistaken for a digging tool. It is a very stiff sock.

interaction_one_rule.narration: Act out the one rule together: take what the mountain drops, never pry at what it holds. Everybody adds a part. The grandmother plays the mountain. She is very good at standing still.

interaction.cue: Each hero acts a part of the one rule.

options.label: Pretend to pick up a fallen pebble
options.reaction: You pick up what fell freely. The grandmother mountain nods.

options.label: Show why the pry bar must stop
options.reaction: You stop the pretend pry bar before it touches the grandmother mountain.

options.label: Be the mountain holding something safe
options.reaction: You hold your hands closed. The prospector finally watches what the rule means.

onSuccess.narration: The prospector watches the whole play. Then he lowers his pry bar and asks where to leave it.

onFailure.narration: He nods along, says "Right, right," and marches up the hill with his pry bar anyway. You follow him, because somebody should.

onAssisted.narration: The grandmother adds the missing part. Together you show the rule, and the prospector lowers his bar.

interaction_crab_warning.narration: Watch the crab's warning: claws up, shuffle sideways, leave the warm patch. Copy it in order, so the prospector can see how to back away.

interaction.cue: Watch the warning, then echo the safe response in order.

onSuccess.narration: You copy the warning and lead everyone off the warm patch.

onFailure.narration: You decide the dance means hello. It does not mean hello.

onAssisted.narration: The prospector copies your first two steps. Together you back off the warm ground.

interaction_kept_stone.narration: Ashby will let you carry the stone if you keep its wrapping level. Raise or lower your side, then lift it gently.

interaction.cue: Level the wrapped stone before lifting it from the list.
interaction.objectLabel: The Unassigned Stone in its wrapping

onSuccess.narration: You lift the wrapped stone, perfectly level. Ashby nods. The Unassigned Stone is yours to carry north.

onFailure.narration: Your fingers bump the list crooked. Ashby pats your hand. "You'll know the difference soon. Not today." The stone stays on its list.

onAssisted.narration: Ashby steadies the wrapping with her stick. You lift the stone, and she lets you carry it north.

interaction_dawn_rope.narration: Brace the big bell's rope while one of you guides the pull. Alone, use the cleat. The expert teaches the crew's hand-to-hand passing line. Her clipboard is nearly as tall as she is.

interaction.cue: Hold the rope supports while the acting hero guides the dawn pull.

onSuccess.narration: The dawn bell rings out clean. You practice the passing line.

onFailure.narration: The rope swings back up and takes you with it. For one glorious moment you are flying. Then the grandmothers catch your ankles, and the bell rings anyway.

onAssisted.narration: A grandmother sets the cleat beside you. You ring the dawn bell and practice the line.

interaction_crowd_bell_line.narration: Pass a signal bell hand to hand down your crew line, to the grandmothers at the gate. Then they can call each row forward without any pushing.

interaction.cue: Catch the signal bell and pass it toward the gate.

onSuccess.narration: The bell reaches the gate. The grandmothers call the crowd forward row by row, and the pushing stops.

onFailure.narration: A grandmother catches the bell before it drops. She calls the rows while you keep the gap clear.

onAssisted.narration: A grandmother fills the gap beside you. The bell gets through, and the crowd settles.

interaction_crowd_hand_bells.narration: Fit your polished bells between the grandmothers' notes, a turn each. Each chime calls a row forward. The feathered hat has to stop shouting to hear his row.

interaction.cue: Each hero adds a hand-bell answer to the prepared chorus.

options.label: Answer after the low bell
options.reaction: Your answer follows the low bell. The next row waits for its turn.

options.label: Answer after the high bell
options.reaction: Your answer follows the high bell. The expert waves one row forward.

options.label: Leave a space for the next answer
options.reaction: You leave a clear space. The waiting crowd hears the next little bell.

onSuccess.narration: The chorus gives each row its turn. The crowd settles, with room around the stones.

onFailure.narration: The expert fills in the missing note. The crowd settles while you keep the space clear.

onAssisted.narration: The expert guides your chimes. Together you settle the crowd.

interaction_crowd_account.narration: The grandmothers make room by the cart for your story. Share something you saw, or ask for a tally to be read. The feathered hat is running out of breath.

interaction_gear_inventory_response_show.narration: The grandmother checks what you show against her tally. She writes down your gear and waves you through.

interaction_gear_inventory_response_use.narration: She writes each use beside each thing. The sock gets a question mark. Then she waves you through.

interaction_gear_inventory_response_chec.narration: She checks one pocket at a time with you, waiting for your answers. Then she writes it all down and waves you through.

interaction_crowd_account_response_moths.narration: You tell them about the moths going south. The grandmothers pass your words down the line. The crowd listens, and the pushing stops.

interaction_crowd_account_response_talli.narration: Ashby reads the broken pattern aloud. The feathered hat stops to hear the numbers. The grandmothers pass it down the line, and the pushing stops.

interaction_crowd_account_response_rule.narration: You explain what the mountain drops and what it holds. Somebody lowers a digging tool. The grandmothers pass your words down the line, and the pushing stops.

voiceGuide.tone: warm, loud dragonling home country under a worried sky; grandmothers in charge, bells everywhere, a little spooky about the unrung bell, never scary

npcVoices.great_gran_ashby: the oldest dragonling grandmother; brisk, tender, unarguable, taps things with her walking stick
npcVoices.grandmother: a gate-town grandmother; glasses on a chain, counts everything, hugs first and inspects later
npcVoices.small_dragonling: a bell-code expert aged about six; talks at top speed until the unrung bell comes up
npcVoices.prospector: a stubborn rush prospector with a pry bar; says 'right, right' and doesn't listen until he does
npcVoices.perrin: Perrin Nine-Verse, a centaur guide; conspiratorial, emotional, desperate the Shortcut stays an argument
npcVoices.wend: a Deep Hollow ladler from the north road; gentle, generous, remembers every name, certain the world can be fixed at the root
npcVoices.sergeant_holloway: a Skywarden supply sergeant from the north road; rigid, honest, calls everything 'arithmetic', writes everything down
npcVoices.feathered_hat: a loud prospector on a cart; blustering, sure the stones are just old rocks, quiet once he really listens

interaction_pry_bars.narration: Prospectors hand over pry bars at the stones. Pass them up the slope to the grandmothers' wall. A grandmother has left room for the huge one. She is an optimist.

interaction.cue: Catch the pry bar, then pass it up the line.

onSuccess.narration: The last pry bar reaches the wall with a clunk, and the grandmother hangs it up, very pleased. "Wall-hanging rate," she says, and counts three coins into your hands. "Honest work, honestly paid."

onFailure.narration: One pry bar slips, and a prospector catches it with his boot. "Ow," he says, bravely. The line laughs, and the pry bars go on up the hill.

onAssisted.narration: The grandmother takes the heavy end herself, and together you pass the pry bars up the slope without a single clunk. She counts three coins into your hands. "Wall-hanging rate," she says.

interaction_bell_tuck.narration: Help tuck the bells in with soft cloths so they will not ring in the night. "Company helps," says Ashby. A little bell gives a sleepy ting before you reach it.

interaction.cue: Tuck the bells in for the night, any way you like.

options.label: Drape a cloth over a bell
options.reaction: The bell settles with a very small, sleepy tink.

options.label: Hum a bell lullaby
options.reaction: Every bell on the rafters hums along, softly.

options.label: Give one a last polish
options.reaction: The bell shines, and you can see your sleepy face in it.

stages: Most of the bells are tucked in.
The whole bell house is hushed.

onSuccess.narration: The last bell goes quiet, and the whole bell house breathes out. A grandmother tucks a bundle of leftover bread into your pack. "Breakfast," she whispers. "Bells sleep better when guests are fed."

onFailure.narration: One small bell goes ting at the very last second. Forty grandmothers say shhh at once, and then they all giggle, and the bell house settles down for the night anyway.

interaction_gear_inventory.narration: Lay out what your hero carries and say what each thing is for. The grandmother checks beside you. One sock has been mistaken for a digging tool. It is a particularly stiff sock.

interaction.cue: Each hero names a real item and explains its use.

options.label: Show what I carry
options.reaction: The grandmother checks the things you show against her tally.

options.label: Explain what my gear is for
options.reaction: She writes the uses beside the gear. The sock receives a question mark.

options.label: Ask her to check with me
options.reaction: She helps check one pocket at a time, leaving room for your answer.

onSuccess.narration: The grandmother finishes checking the packs. She records your actual gear and waves you through.

onFailure.narration: You lay it all out, but your packs are still ringing like a shop door. The grandmother inspects everything anyway, including your socks, and writes PROBABLY HONEST in the tally book. Then she hugs you, because that is what grandmothers do after an inspection.

onAssisted.narration: The grandmother helps name the gear, then records what you showed. The inspection is complete.

interaction_crowd_account.narration: The grandmothers make a place beside the cart for your account. Each hero shares something witnessed here, or asks for one of the tallies to be read. You do not have to outshout the feathered hat. The hat is running out of breath.

interaction.cue: Each hero shares evidence or asks for a tally to be read.

options.label: Describe the moths we saw leaving
options.reaction: Your account of the southbound moths gives the waiting people something to listen to.

options.label: Ask Ashby to read the changed tallies
options.reaction: Ashby reads the broken pattern aloud. The feathered hat stops to hear the numbers.

options.label: Explain the boundary rule in my own words
options.reaction: You explain what is freely dropped and what must stay held. A listener lowers a digging tool.

onSuccess.narration: The grandmothers repeat your account down the line. The crowd listens, and the pushing stops.

onFailure.narration: You climb up and start to tell them, and the crowd shouts you down. But while they are shouting at you, nobody is pushing. By the time they run out of breath, the grandmothers have rung for help, and twenty more grandmothers have arrived. The crowd sits down, grumbling.

onAssisted.narration: Ashby helps read the evidence beside you. Together you give the crowd an account it can hear.
